title: Trash zone: delete when the Note overlaps it, not the pointer
lede: A drop now deletes when the dragged **Note's rect overlaps the Trash zone**, touching edges included, wherever the pointer is. Before, only the pointer counted, so a large Note held by its far edge could cover most of the zone and still be moved. The Preview rect is in Board coordinates and the zone in client coordinates, so the controller passes the **Board's origin on screen**: measured at press, moved by the scroll since. The highlight (`overTrash`) and the release (`commit`) ask the same function, so the highlight always predicts what a release does.

files.question: When does a release delete instead of move?
files.summary: `noteOverTrash` places the move's Preview rect on screen with `ctx.boardOrigin` and tests it against the zone with `intersects`. `overTrash` and `commit` both call it.
files.owns: The hit rule: the Note's rect, edges included; the pointer plays no part.
files.never: Measures the DOM or reads the scroll: the zone and the Board's origin arrive in the `DragContext`.
files.tested: Node tests in `kinds.test.ts`; each Trash zone case checks `overTrash` and `commit` together.

files.question: When do two rects overlap?
files.summary: `intersects(a, b)`: an axis-aligned box test, touching edges counting as overlap, the same rule `contains` uses.
files.never: Knows about the Trash zone or the screen.
files.tested: Node tests in `geometry.test.ts`: overlap, touching edges, one inside the other, apart on each axis.

files.question: Where is the Board on screen at each move?
files.summary: A press measures the zone and the Board's origin once, for a kind with `overTrash`. `context` gives the kind the origin less the scroll since the press, the same scroll `delta` adds.
files.owns: The `DragContext` and the order of the Trash zone writes.
files.never: Touches the DOM: `boardOrigin` is read through `DragIO`.
files.tested: Node tests against a recording fake `DragIO`, including a scroll mid-drag.

files.question: Where does the Board's origin come from?
files.summary: The real `boardOrigin` reads the Board element's `getBoundingClientRect`, through the new `boardRef`.

A resize gets `null` and a zero origin it never reads. The Board ref is new in `BoardDomContext`, because `useDrag` now needs the Board element itself, not only its scroll container.

steps.explain: Each update builds the context and asks the kind. `noteOverTrash` takes the same rect the Preview shows (`moved`: rounded and clamped to the Board), moves it by the Board's origin into client coordinates, and tests it against the zone. scenarios.name: A Note released beside the zone, 10 px short of it

steps.title: pointerup with the Note's right edge left of the zone
steps.explain: The rects are apart on the x axis, so `intersects` is false: the zone stayed `armed` and the release is an ordinary `move` to the rect the Preview showed. One more pixel to the right and the edges would touch, which counts as overlap (`kinds.test.ts` checks both: 1 px apart moves, touching deletes).

scenarios.name: The Board scrolls during the Drag

steps.title: scroll with the pointer still
steps.explain: The Board slides up and left under the pointer, and `delta` adds the scroll so the Note follows the pointer, not the Board. Its Board position grows by the scroll while the Board's origin on screen shrinks by the same amount, so the Note's client rect stays put and the zone's state doesn't change. Without the correction in `context`, the Note would be measured as if it had moved by the scroll: the controller test and the browser test both fail if it is removed (checked by deleting it).

steps.title: Why the scroll still matters at the Board's edge
steps.explain: When the delta and the scroll cancel out, the scroll seems not to matter. It matters once the Preview is clamped to the Board: the clamped rect no longer follows the pointer, and only the Board's real origin places it correctly on screen. `kinds.test.ts` covers this with a Note pushed past the Board's bottom edge, over the zone only when the Board is scrolled.

notes.title: This reverses the old "brushing moves" rule
notes.detail: #6 chose the pointer on purpose, so a large Note brushing the zone was moved, and the earlier interaction prototype marks overlap as rejected. The client reviewer read that as "not meeting" the requirement: you drag the Note to the trash, not the pointer. The counter-argument still stands: a large Note near the bottom-right can now be deleted by accident. Undo is the safety net, and the highlight warns before the release.

notes.title: Touching counts
notes.detail: The issue asked for the same edge rule as `contains`, so a Note whose edge lies exactly on the zone's edge is deleted. The rects are in fractional client pixels, so this is a single-pixel line in practice.

notes.title: Measured at press, not at every move
notes.detail: The Board's origin could be read with `getBoundingClientRect` on every move, which would need no scroll arithmetic. Measuring once matches how the zone is measured, keeps layout reads out of the hot path, and keeps the controller testable with a fake `DragIO`.

notes.title: `contains` has no production caller now
notes.detail: It was used only by the old pointer rule. It is kept, with its tests, as the stated edge rule `intersects` follows. Delete it if you prefer.

notes.title: A Board ref after all
notes.detail: The #6 walkthrough noted that nothing read a Board ref, so `BoardDomContext` had none. `useDrag` now needs one, so `Board` takes its ref from the context instead of its own `useRef`.
